ja: 彼女は途中で 2 回道に迷ったけど、今はもうホテルを見つけました。
en: She got lost twice on the way, but she's found the hotel now.
alternatives: She got lost twice on the way, but now she's found the hotel.
She got lost two times on the way, but she's found her hotel now.
point: 過去の出来事は過去形、今の結果は現在完了で分ける

ja: 私たち、このあたりをもう30分も歩き回ってるんです。駅はどっちですか？
en: We've been walking around this area for thirty minutes already. Which way is the station?
alternatives: We've been walking around here for half an hour. Which way is the station?
We've been walking around here for thirty minutes now. How do we get to the station?
point: 今も続く「ずっと〜している」は have been -ing

ja: すみません、市立図書館を探しているんですが。
en: Excuse me, I'm looking for the city library.
alternatives: Excuse me, I'm trying to find the city library.
Sorry, I'm looking for the city library.
point: 「探している」は今している最中なので進行形 I'm looking for

ja: 私、ホテルを出る前に地図アプリをダウンロードしておけばよかった。
en: I wish I'd downloaded a map app before I left the hotel.
alternatives: If only I had downloaded a map app before leaving the hotel.
I should have downloaded a map app before I left the hotel.
point: 過去への後悔は I wish の後を過去完了 had done にする

ja: フロントの人に、駅までの行き方を紙に書いてくれるよう頼んでもらえますか？
en: Could you ask the front desk staff to write down directions to the station for me?
alternatives: Can you ask the front desk staff to write down how to get to the station?
Could you ask someone at the front desk to write the directions to the station on a piece of paper?
point: ask 人 to do で「人に〜するよう頼む」

ja: すみません、ここから一番近い駅への行き方を教えていただけますか？
en: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the nearest station from here?
alternatives: Excuse me, would you mind telling me how to get to the nearest station from here?
Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the nearest station?
point: 「行き方」は how to get to で、get の後の to を落とさない

ja: 駅の近くにバス停が二つありますよ。
en: There are two bus stops near the station.
alternatives: You'll find two bus stops near the station.
Near the station, there are two bus stops.
point: 複数あるときは There are と複数形の stops

ja: ここから旧市街まで、どう行くのが一番いいですか？
en: What's the best way to get to the old town from here?
alternatives: How should I get to the old town from here?
What's the best way to get from here to the old town?
point: 「一番いい行き方」は the best way to get to

ja: すみません、この近くにコンビニはありますか？
en: Excuse me, is there a convenience store nearby?
alternatives: Excuse me, is there a convenience store near here?
Excuse me, is there a convenience store around here?
point: 「ありますか」は Is there で始める

ja: 駅へ行く道は、工事のため今は通行止めになっています。
en: The road to the station has been closed for construction.
alternatives: The road to the station is closed because of construction.
The road to the station has been closed due to construction work.
point: 「〜されている」状態は has been closed / is closed の受動態

ja: 私がどうしても知りたいのは、この時間でも駅までのバスがまだ走っているかどうかなんです。
en: What I really need to know is whether there's still a bus running to the station at this hour.
alternatives: What I really want to know is whether a bus still runs to the station at this time of night.
The thing I really need to know is if there's still a bus to the station at this hour.
point: 「〜かどうか」は whether 節、語順は平叙文のまま

ja: すみません、この辺りに両替所はありますか？それとも一番近いのは駅の中ですか？
en: Excuse me, is there a currency exchange around here, or is the nearest one inside the station?
alternatives: Excuse me, is there somewhere to exchange money near here, or is the closest one in the station?
Sorry, is there a currency exchange office nearby, or is the nearest one inside the station?
point: 初めて話題にする両替所は a、一つに決まる「一番近い」は the

ja: すみません、この住所が地図のどのあたりなのか、それと歩いて行ける距離なのかどうか教えていただけますか？
en: Excuse me, could you tell me where this address is on the map and whether it's within walking distance?
alternatives: Excuse me, could you show me where this address is on the map and tell me if I can walk there?
Sorry, could you tell me where this address is on the map and if it's walkable?
point: where this address is の語順。is を前に出さない

ja: スマホの充電が切れていなければ自分で調べるんですが、駅までの行き方を教えてもらえますか？
en: If my phone weren't dead, I'd look it up myself, but could you tell me how to get to the station?
alternatives: If my phone had any battery left, I'd check it myself, but could you tell me the way to the station?
I'd look it up myself if my phone weren't dead, but could you tell me how to get to the station?
point: 今の事実に反する仮定なので weren't と I'd を使う

ja: すみません、この近くに駅まで行くバスがあるかどうか、教えていただけないかと思いまして。
en: Excuse me, I was wondering if you could tell me whether there's a bus around here that goes to the station.
alternatives: Excuse me, would you mind telling me if there's a bus near here that goes to the station?
Sorry to bother you, but could you tell me if there's a bus around here that goes to the station?
point: whether の後は there's の語順。is there にしない

ja: その場所、地図で見せてもらえますか？
en: Can you show me on the map?
alternatives: Could you show me on the map?
Can you show me where it is on the map?
point: show の後に me を忘れない

ja: すみません、この近くで SIM カードが買える場所を知りませんか？
en: Excuse me, do you know a place near here where I can buy a SIM card?
alternatives: Excuse me, do you know anywhere near here where I can buy a SIM card?
Excuse me, do you know of a place around here where I could buy a SIM card?
point: 場所を説明する関係詞は where で、後ろは完全な文

ja: 美術館はこの通りの突き当たりにありますよ。
en: The museum is at the end of this street.
alternatives: The museum is at the end of this road.
The museum is where this street ends.
point: 「突き当たりに」は at the end of で表す

ja: さっき道を聞いた男の人が、その橋は通行止めだから遠回りしないといけないって言ってたよ。
en: The man I asked earlier said the bridge was closed, so we'd have to take a detour.
alternatives: The guy I asked for directions earlier said the bridge was closed and we would need to take a detour.
The man I asked a minute ago told me the bridge was closed, so we'd have to go the long way around.
point: 時制の一致で is→was、will have to→would have to にする

ja: 道がわからなければ、ホテルのフロントの人に地図に印をつけてもらうといいですよ。
en: If you're not sure of the way, you could have the front desk mark it on a map for you.
alternatives: If you don't know the way, you could get the front desk to mark it on a map for you.
If you're unsure of the way, why not have the front desk mark it on a map for you?
point: have＋人＋動詞の原形。get なら get＋人＋to 不定詞になる

ja: ホテルが見つからないなら、彼らは一つ手前の駅で降りるべきだったんだと思うよ。
en: If they can't find the hotel, I think they should have gotten off one stop earlier.
alternatives: If they can't find the hotel, I think they should have gotten off at the previous stop.
If they can't find the hotel, they probably should've gotten off a stop earlier.
point: 過去にすべきだったことは should have + 過去分詞

ja: 私は地図アプリを使うより、地元の人に道を聞くほうが好きなんです。
en: I prefer asking locals for directions to using a map app.
alternatives: I'd rather ask locals for directions than use a map app.
I like asking locals for directions better than using a map app.
point: prefer A to B は A も B も動名詞でそろえる

ja: あの駅員さんに道を聞いていなかったら、私たちは逆方向の電車に乗っていたよ。
en: If we hadn't asked that station attendant for directions, we would have gotten on a train going the opposite way.
alternatives: If we hadn't asked that station worker for directions, we'd have taken a train in the wrong direction.
If we hadn't asked that station attendant, we would've gotten on the wrong train.
point: 過去の仮定は had not asked、帰結は would have gotten

ja: さっきあの角を左に曲がってたら、私たち今ごろもうホテルに着いてたのにね。
en: If we'd turned left at that corner earlier, we'd already be at the hotel by now.
alternatives: If we had taken a left at that corner, we'd be at the hotel by now.
We'd already be at the hotel if we'd turned left back at that corner.
point: 過去の仮定で今の結果なので後半は would be

ja: その女性は地図を確認しながら、駅から美術館までの行き方を丁寧に説明してくれました。
en: The woman carefully explained how to get from the station to the museum, checking the map as she went.
alternatives: The woman explained carefully how to get from the station to the museum while checking the map.
The woman checked the map as she carefully explained the way from the station to the museum.
point: 「〜しながら」は文末に , checking のように -ing を添える

ja: 美術館は駅から少し遠いけど、川沿いを歩いていけば迷わずに着けますよ。
en: Although the museum is a bit far from the station, you can't miss it if you walk along the river.
alternatives: Even though the museum's a bit far from the station, you won't get lost if you follow the river.
The museum is a bit far from the station, but if you walk along the river, you can't miss it.
point: Although を使ったら後半に but は付けない

ja: すみません、この辺りに両替できる所があるか教えていただけますか？
en: Excuse me, could you tell me if there's a place around here where I can exchange some money?
alternatives: Excuse me, could you tell me whether there's somewhere nearby where I can exchange money?
Excuse me, would you happen to know if there's a place around here where I can change money?
point: 「〜できる所」は a place where I can と where でつなぐ

ja: よかったら、私が駅まで案内しますよ。
en: I'll take you to the station if you like.
alternatives: I'll show you the way to the station if you like.
I can take you to the station if you want.
point: その場で決めた申し出は will を使う

ja: 橋を渡ったら、交差点が見えるまでまっすぐ進んでください。
en: After you cross the bridge, keep going straight until you see an intersection.
alternatives: Once you cross the bridge, go straight until you see an intersection.
When you cross the bridge, keep walking straight until you see an intersection.
point: after 節も until 節も未来の話だが現在形

ja: 駅員さんが私に教えてくれた道は、あなたがさっき言っていた道とは違いました。
en: The route the station staff told me about was different from the one you mentioned earlier.
alternatives: The directions the station staff gave me were different from the ones you mentioned earlier.
The way the station staff showed me was different from the one you mentioned earlier.
point: 主語が長い名詞句でも動詞 was を見失わない
